A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gradient Slingshots and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization, with no essential evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 experiments, including manipulation results, model-size comparisons, and evaluations of proposed defenses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds an ImageNet manipulation example using a pretrained Wide ResNet50 in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The implemented method retains the gradient target γ(s−x), slingshot and landing regions, and weighted manipulation and preservation losses. The ImageNet example applies the same method with different settings; discussion of broader optimization algorithms does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds manipulation and evaluation on higher-dimensional ImageNet images, extending the retained toy, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 coverage. v1's use of an ImageNet fish image as a manipulation target and ImageNet-pretrained LPIPS features did not constitute this evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The optimizer comparison retains exactly None, GC, TR, Adam, and Adam+GC+TR in v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 6. Original-model comparisons also remain. The α=1 condition was already represented in v1's appendix boxplots.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a separate protocol using 64 ImageNet classes with 600 samples each for preservation and 20 different classes for testing, alongside distinct fine-tuning and AM settings. Appendix B also corrects the reported toy sampling region from the intersection to the union of the zones; this does not establish a rerun. Retained MNIST/CIFAR-10 settings are otherwise stable.

E4.justification: The principal α-sensitivity, model-size, optimizer, and natural-image analyses remain. v2 adds an ImageNet optimization-trajectory failure case, but removes v1's all-output-neuron visualization check in Figure 3 and the MNIST/CIFAR-10 optimization-dynamics analyses in Figures 9–10 and 12–13.

E5.justification: v2 removes the trajectory plots labeled as including confidence intervals and the distribution boxplots from v1 Figures 10–11 and 13–14. Mean-and-standard-deviation table reporting and the 100-AM-sample optimizer comparisons remain; no change in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Retained trade-off values change slightly: MNIST MSE at α=0.01 changes from 0.046 to 0.052. v2 supplies numerical α=1 summaries and replaces sample FVs. Its new ImageNet case reports original-to-manipulated accuracy of 84.13% to 81.86% on the specified test subset and loss of target resemblance after the first step. Model-size and optimizer-comparison table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's incorrect characterization of the displayed negative quadratic g as convex. Otherwise, the quadratic construction, one-step argument, landing-radius bounds, and both proofs are retained, largely relocated to Appendix A; the expanded convergence presentation does not constitute a new proof.

C1.justification: v1 presents protective measures and defense feasibility as a principal contribution in its abstract, introduction, and conclusion. v2 removes that headline contribution while retaining the claim of manipulating visualizations without architectural changes or substantial performance loss.

C2.justification: The retained optimizer experiments are reframed from proposed defenses to preliminary evidence of attack robustness. v2 explicitly limits the central study to unregularized gradient ascent, discusses enlarged manipulation regions for other optimizers, and interprets the new ImageNet trajectory as missing an insufficiently large landing zone, connecting the observed failure to dimensionality and hyperparameter selection.

D1.justification: Appendix F documents the pretrained model source, data subsets, and settings including Adam learning rate 10^-6, γ=200, and zone radii 10^-8. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit PyTorch implementation link and makes the retained dataset-normalization description less specific. The PDFs establish removal of access information, not disappearance of the code itself.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage is substantially narrowed: the local/global/glocal explanation survey and numerous associated citations disappear, while mechanistic-interpretability framing, including Bricken et al., is added. References supporting the new ImageNet/Wide ResNet experiment also appear. The central architectural contrast with Geirhos et al. remains; its publication update is not a new comparison.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Theory and metric explanations move to appendices, defense material is reorganized into Appendix E, natural-image evaluation becomes a main subsection, and limitations receive a separate section. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, combines the main trade-off tables into a scaled-LPIPS summary, relocates full tables, and splits the defense figure into two appendix figures. It removes several diagnostic figures, reformats retained displays, and adds the ImageNet trajectory. The new Table 1 caption incorrectly says MSE although its columns report LPIPS.

improvement.justification: The explicit scope limitations and candid ImageNet failure case make applicability easier to assess, while removing the headline defense contribution better matches the limited defense evidence. These provide a modest improvement in scientific credibility. The gains are constrained by removal of useful optimization and uncertainty diagnostics, loss of the implementation pointer, and the new MSE/LPIPS caption error.
